lower_bound.quote:
A nonnegative integer that
never increases and starts at a positive value can never reach \(0\); hence \(K\ge1\) at
every stage, so at least one nonunit remains at every stage.
lower_bound.witness: COUNTEREXAMPLE: the nonnegative integer sequence 1,0 never increases and starts positive, yet reaches 0. Thus monotonic nonincrease alone does not imply K remains positive. The write-up needed to use the move cases to prove directly that every move leaves at least one output greater than 1.
lower_bound.load_bearing: This is the stated justification that the terminal board is not all 1s. Without a valid argument for at least one surviving nonunit, termination and the at-most-one argument do not establish exactly one survivor.

parsed.notes: The explicit formula and primewise invariant are correct. Termination is valid, but the written proof of existence of a terminal nonunit relies on a false monotonicity inference.
